catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.home.v1 is the closest class, but it carries an optional numeric speed_scale input that AsciiAxis.home() has no argument for; serving it would advertise an input that cannot reach the device. The extension takes no input and reports the native home result.
catalogue_requests.summary: Send the native home command and wait until the axis reports idle.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 fixes joint positions in radians; the clone addresses the axis in integer microsteps and names no microstep-to-length calibration, so a rad binding would invent a conversion. The extension keeps the native microstep unit and marks its travel operator_required.
catalogue_requests.summary: Move the axis to an absolute native position in microsteps and wait until idle.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class expresses a relative move in the device's native integer microstep unit; the catalogue motion classes fix positions in radians and the clone names no microstep-to-length calibration. The extension keeps the native unit and marks its distance operator_required.
catalogue_requests.summary: Move the axis by a relative distance in microsteps and wait until idle.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_velocity.v1 fixes velocities in rad/s; the clone sends an integer native speed and names neither a unit nor a range for it. A rad/s binding would invent a conversion; the extension keeps the native value and marks its speed operator_required.
catalogue_requests.summary: Start continuous motion at a native speed; call stop to end it.

catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.stop.v1 carries an optional numeric deceleration input that AsciiAxis.stop() has no argument for; serving it would advertise an input that cannot reach the device. The extension takes no input, reports the native stop, and is the declared safe-state action.
catalogue_requests.summary: Stop the axis with the native stop command and wait until it reports idle.

Model-authored and unreviewed: no hardware run; the fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording, and native.py was not run. The package binds only the ASCII protocol entry AsciiAxis; the card's BinaryDevice/BinarySerial entry symbols exist in the clone but the binary protocol is NOT COVERED, and the package serves one configured axis. The clone states no travel range, no speed unit or range and no force limit, so every numeric motion input is Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json holds example numbers only (placeholders, not a statement about any device), and the fake and fixture numbers are test data. The native stop AsciiAxis.stop() is the e-stop; x-cap.ksunden.stop.v1 is the safe-state action. No independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so no estop_physical_ref is set (the driver is R1). gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
